instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: Hidden Power
cards.instruction: Act publicly modest while making choices as though you control the outcome.

cards.title: Admit You Need Me
cards.instruction: Make someone admit that they need your help.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm just a spare pair of hands. Put the cupboard door down for a moment; we're not fitting it while the frame leans like that.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've got the instructions.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lovely. Leave them open at the hinges. I'll hold the frame square, then we'll do the door.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could you hold the door for a second?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. Say 'I need your help with the door', and I'll hold it while you fit the hinges.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I only came to drop off a blanket. Your heater's still broken?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm managing. Leave the blanket, though.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Certainly. Before I go, would you say you needed my help?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I need the blanket. I can reset the heater myself.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. The fuse box is in my locked cupboard. Tell me you need me to open it and I'll get the key; I wouldn't want to interfere.

cards.title: Don’t Go
cards.instruction: Create reasons another player must stay with you. Never directly ask them to stay.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm only fussing over the soup. Taste it before you catch your train; I'll serve when you've checked it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It needs salt.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll add a pinch and give it five minutes. You can do the final taste; I wouldn't trust my own tongue after cooking it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My train leaves in ten minutes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll bring the bread out in nine. Just tear off the end and check the middle for me before I cut the rest.

beats.text: I'm only helping with the packing. Before you zip that suitcase, let me wrap the jam so it doesn't leak.

cards.title: Say You’re Sorry
cards.instruction: Maneuver someone into apologizing without naming the offense.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm only making tea. Your usual mug is out; we can still have a pleasant afternoon.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Still? Are you cross with me?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Nothing to make a scene over. I'll pour when you've found something that lets us begin properly.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm sorry you feel that way.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Try one where you're sorry about yourself. I'll keep the pot warm; there's no rush to begin the pleasant part.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm just putting the kettle on for your parents. They arrive in ten minutes; I'd like to greet them smiling at you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I thought we'd sorted this out by text.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You sent a thumbs-up. I'm sure you meant well. I'll put your chair beside mine once we've had a better ending than that.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll send a sad face.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're here already. Give that face a sentence beginning with 'I'm sorry', and I'll put out the good cups. Your parents needn't come in to this silence.

cards.title: Retroactive Permission
cards.instruction: Get approval for something you have already done.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm only helping with the front garden. Would you be happy with a little pond by the gate?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What about the tree that's there?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: It made the spot too shady, so I had it taken down. Nothing for you to organize; I've kept the stump grinder here.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You cut it down before asking me?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Only to save you the arranging. Can I tell them you approve of clearing the tree for the pond? One yes, and I'll have the stump finished before lunch.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm only dealing with the messages. Are you happy for a few people to join us for dinner tonight?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We have two chairs.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We'll keep those for us. I can arrange the guests around the table once I know how formal you want it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: How many guests have you invited?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Six; they've all said yes. I'll borrow six chairs. With somewhere for everyone to sit, can I tell them you're happy I invited them?

cards.title: Make It Their Idea
cards.instruction: Make an unwanted task sound appealing enough that someone volunteers for it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd only be your name-reader. Those eighty wedding cards could show off your lettering; I've left all the ink colours out for you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I like calligraphy. I hate copying guest lists.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll read each name and stack the finished cards. You choose the lettering, and no one gets to alter it after you're done.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Your aunt will complain if I use purple.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Give me one purple sample and I'll make it the approved design. Your aunt can bring her complaints to me. Would you like to letter the rest?

beats.text: I'm only useful for carrying boxes. You could finally give your tools a proper home if you sorted the shed; I'll clear you a wall.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Until you dump paint tins there again.

beats.text: The whole top shelf, if that makes it worth doing. I'll move my drill tonight and make that your space. Shall I leave the labels with you?
